llm.summary: This image-generation skill is not clearly malicious, but it includes a broad paid API marketplace client that can use the user's API key beyond the advertised nano-banana image workflow.

dimensions.detail: Network access and an API key are expected for this service, but marketplace-wide enumeration, task-history access, schema export, and custom-host support are broader than necessary for a narrow image skill.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: There is no dependency install, remote code retrieval, or automatic execution; setup asks the user to run the Python client and provide an API key. The docs also suggest obtaining support/API-key help through a personal WeChat contact, which users should treat cautiously.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The main skill instructions emphasize api.a7w.cn and nano_banana, while the CLI exposes arbitrary app/api arguments and a host override; those broad controls are only partially disclosed and are not tightly scoped to the image use case.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The login command persistently stores the user API key in ~/.a7w/config.json with an attempted 0600 permission setting; this is disclosed and there is no background service, but it is still sensitive credential persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose centers on two nano_banana image endpoints, but scripts/client.py can list all available apps, dump schemas, inspect tasks/usage, and call any app/API allowed by the user's token.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this before installing if you only want a narrow nano-banana image tool. Use a dedicated low-balance API key, avoid --host/A7W_HOST unless you fully trust the endpoint, do not share keys through chat, and be aware the client can access other marketplace apps and recent task metadata available to that key.
llm.findings:
[TT3] expected: The code does send the user's API key in an Authorization header to the configured service, which is expected for API authentication; I did not find artifact-backed evidence that it secretly sends credentials elsewhere, though the host override weakens the 'api.a7w.cn only' claim.
[TP4] unexpected: The broad marketplace client materially exceeds the advertised two-endpoint nano_banana purpose, so this concern is supported by the artifact.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The arbitrary call interface, app listing, schema dump, and account task/usage queries are real broader capabilities, not limited to the image workflow.
[E1] expected: Outbound requests to api.a7w.cn are central to the skill, but users should be cautious about the informal WeChat/API-key support path and any custom host configuration.
[LP3] unexpected: The package uses prose permission descriptions rather than enforceable scope, which matters because the shipped client is more general than the skill description.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The callback_url and schema dump behaviors are disclosed at a basic level but lack clear warnings about third-party callback data and local persistence of exported schemas.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-only documentation is a usability and reviewability limitation, but I did not use it as a security basis for the verdict.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The activation boundaries are loose for a skill that can invoke paid external APIs, adding to the scoping concern.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The whoami/points descriptions are somewhat inconsistent with implementation details, but this is a secondary documentation issue rather than evidence of malicious behavior.
